result.message:
Deliver patch-2 (v5): symlinked directories are collected again.

Source fix (src/_pytest/pathlib.py, `visit()`): `entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)` → `entry.is_dir()`, removing the 6.1.0 regression from b473e515 so a symlink to a directory inside a collected directory is followed and collected as before. Other callers (collection entry points, fnmatch/rootdir handling with plain paths) are unaffected.

Regression test (testing/test_collection.py::test_collect_symlink_dir): builds `real/test_real.py` plus directory symlink `symlink_to_real -> real`, and asserts BOTH `real/test_real.py::test_real` and `symlink_to_real/test_real.py::test_real` are collected and PASSED with exit code 0.

Evidence the test discriminates: with the fix reverted, this test alone fails (1 collected, 1 failed, 0 passed — report test-report-b4914457516f7caad01b7c5a); with the fix in place it passes.

Current-version (v5) public run: testing/test_collection.py + testing/test_pathlib.py → 142 collected, 141 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed, 0 errors (report test-report-261c474cf84fd7110b4f6f12). Earlier same-change run of test_collection.py alone: 80 collected, 79 passed, 1 xfailed (test-report-c00e24e5d81a0f821dbf3c66).

Not verified: only these two modules ran; the remainder of the public suite was not executed on this version, and no hidden acceptance was run. A passing public run is not hidden acceptance.
